'''''Hymenocallis speciosa''''', the '''green-tinge spiderlily''', is a [[species]] of the genus ''[[Hymenocallis]]'' that is native to the [[Windward Islands]] in the eastern [[Caribbean]]. It is cultivated as an ornamental in some areas, and reportedly naturalized in [[Cuba]] and the [[Bahamas]].<ref name="smith">{{cite web|url=http://botany.si.edu/Antilles/WestIndies/getonerecord.cfm?ID=324|publisher=Department of Botany, National Museum of Natural History, Smithsonian Institution|title=Hymenocallis speciosa|accessdate=5 September 2012}}</ref><ref>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=278909 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families, ''Hymenocallis speciosa'']</ref>

''Hymenocallis speciosa'' is a bulb-forming perennial. [[Stipe (botany)|Stipe]] can attain a height of up to 50 cm. Leaves are lanceolate, up to 50 cm long and 10 cm across, narrowing to a [[Petiole (botany)|petiole]] below. One [[umbel]] can produce as many as 20 flowers. Flowers are white with a slight greenish tinge, the [[tepals]] [[reflexed]] (curling backwards) at flowering time.<ref>[http://en.hortipedia.com/wiki/Hymenocallis_speciosa Hortipedia, ''Hymenocallis speciosa'']</ref><ref>Salisbury, Richard Anthony. 1812. Transactions of the Horticultural Society of London 1: 340, ''Hymenocallis speciosa''</ref><ref>[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/759916#page/92/mode/1up Salisbury, Richard Anthony. 1794.  Transactions of the Linnean Society of London 2: 73, t. 12. ''Pancratium speciosum'']</ref><ref>[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/7430516#page/368/mode/1up Rafinesque, Constantine Samuel. 1838. Flora Telluriana 4: 22, ''Nemepiodon speciosum'']</ref>
